title: Symphony No. 6 in B minor, “Pathétique”
hook: A symphony that ends not in triumph but in silence.

painting.title: Above Eternal Peace
painting.pairingNote: Painted a year after the symphony, a vast Russian landscape of stillness and mortality.

facts: Written between February and August 1893 and dedicated to his nephew, Vladimir Davydov.
First performed on 28 October 1893 in St Petersburg, conducted by Tchaikovsky. He died nine days later.
The Russian title means “passionate” or “full of feeling”, not “pathetic”.
Tchaikovsky reverses the usual order: the thrilling march comes third, and the slow movement comes last.
He said the symphony had a secret story, and never revealed it.
bigPicture.inOneLine: struggle and longing (I), a graceful dance with a limp (II), a false victory (III), acceptance and fading (IV).

movements.heading: Adagio – Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: The heart of the symphony. A restless theme born in darkness meets the most famous, warmest melody Tchaikovsky ever wrote. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]: the themes are introduced, thrown into conflict, and brought back.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, unrest
mainIdeas.description: a short, climbing, questioning [[motif|motif]]. First on a lone bassoon in slow motion, then fast and nervous in the violas.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2, longing
mainIdeas.description: a broad melody that drifts downward on [[muted|muted]] strings. The first moment of light.

stops.hear: A single bassoon over dark, hollow double basses
stops.happening: The introduction. The seed of Theme 1, in slow motion

stops.hear: Violas play the same idea, fast and anxious; strings and woodwinds trade phrases
stops.happening: The main section begins with Theme 1. Tension climbs step by step

stops.hear: Everything calms; a wide, singing melody on muted strings
stops.happening: Theme 2. The signature tune of the symphony

stops.hear: Flute and bassoon in conversation over a pulsing string accompaniment
stops.happening: The middle of Theme 2, a little more animated

stops.hear: The famous melody returns in the full orchestra
stops.happening: Theme 2 at its fullest

stops.hear: A solo clarinet lets the melody fade to almost nothing
stops.happening: Tchaikovsky writes pppppp here, the quietest marking in the score

stops.hear: A sudden, violent crash; then fast, chasing string passages
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. Theme 1 is torn apart

stops.label: Mid-development
stops.hear: A slow, hymn-like phrase in trombones and trumpets
stops.happening: A quotation from the Russian Orthodox funeral service

stops.hear: Theme 1 returns inside the storm; trombones descend step by step over rolling timpani
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]] and the climax fused together. The most tragic moment

stops.hear: The famous melody comes back, brighter
stops.happening: Theme 2, now in B major: the same tune, but like peace that has been earned

stops.hear: Strings pluck a slowly falling scale; above it, a calm brass [[chorale|chorale]]
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]], with the strings in [[pizzicato|pizzicato]]. The storm has passed; the ending is peaceful, but it points downward

notice: The bassoon idea in the introduction and the viola theme of the Allegro are the same notes; only the speed changes.
Theme 2 comes three times. Compare how the orchestration changes each time.
The falling plucked scale at the end is the first hint of the finale’s “falling line”.

movements.heading: Allegro con grazia
movements.summary: It sounds like a waltz, but it is not one: there are five beats in a bar instead of three. The result is an elegant dance with a slight limp.

stops.hear: A flowing, smiling melody in the cellos over plucked strings
stops.happening: The main section, in D major. A breath after the first movement

stops.hear: The melody moves to woodwinds and violins and is repeated with decoration
stops.happening: The main section expands

stops.hear: The mood darkens: sighing, falling phrases in the violins. Underneath, drums and basses repeat one unchanging note on every beat
stops.happening: The middle section, in B minor. That insistent note is a [[pedal-note|pedal note]], and it sounds like a heartbeat

stops.hear: The first melody returns
stops.happening: The main section comes back

stops.hear: The heartbeat note returns; the melody breaks into fragments and fades
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. The shadow of the middle section falls across the dance

notice: The falling phrases of the middle section are relatives of the first movement’s Theme 2 and of the finale. All of them drift downward.
The repeated single note will return in the double basses at the very end of the symphony.

notes.title: How to hear the rhythm
notes.body: Count “one-two, one-two-three”. Every bar is 2 + 3. After a few bars your ear settles into the lilt.

movements.heading: Allegro molto vivace
movements.summary: A whisper of movement grows, over eight minutes, into a march for the whole orchestra. It sounds like a finale, and audiences often applaud here. But it is a trap; the real ending is still to come.

mainIdeas.description: The [[scherzo|scherzo]] layer: fast, light, never-resting triplets in strings and woodwinds.

mainIdeas.name: The march layer
mainIdeas.description: a hard, leaping tune with a snapped rhythm. At first it appears only in scraps.

stops.hear: Light, quick triplets in the strings; a scrap of march in the oboe
stops.happening: The scherzo begins. The march is only a hint

stops.hear: The scrap travels from instrument to instrument; brass join in
stops.happening: The fragments accumulate

stops.hear: Clarinets play the march from start to finish, still lightly
stops.happening: The first complete statement of the march

stops.hear: The quick triplets start over; a long, patient [[crescendo|crescendo]]
stops.happening: The second round. Tension is stored up

stops.hear: Scales swoop up and down between strings and winds; then the march with cymbals and bass drum
stops.happening: The march in the full orchestra. The goal of the movement

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Hammering chords and rushing descending scales
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. Victory, or something forced? You decide

notice: Even at its brightest, the march is full of falling scales. The finale’s descent is hidden inside the triumph.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Currentzis plays the march as menacing and harsh, not glorious, which makes the collapse of the finale more convincing.

movements.heading: Finale: Adagio lamentoso
movements.summary: Straight after the noise of the march comes this lament, the true conclusion of the symphony. Two falling melodies each try to rise; both collapse; the music dies away in the double basses.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, lament
mainIdeas.description: a cry in the strings, stepping downward.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2, consolation
mainIdeas.description: another falling melody, but warm, over soft pulsing horns.

stops.hear: A falling cry in the strings; bassoons sink into the depths at the end of each phrase
stops.happening: Theme 1

stops.hear: Soft, off-beat pulsing in the horns; above it a warm, falling melody in the strings
stops.happening: Theme 2. It begins quietly and grows with every repetition

stops.hear: The melody reaches a peak, then breaks apart in harsh descending scales; a silence
stops.happening: The first collapse of the consolation

stops.hear: The lament returns, faster and more desperate, and climbs to a great climax
stops.happening: The return of Theme 1 and the summit of the movement

stops.hear: Choked, stopped horn notes; then one soft stroke of a gong
stops.happening: The turning point. The tam-tam plays only this once in the entire symphony

stops.label: Immediately after
stops.hear: Trombones and tuba in slow, hymn-like chords
stops.happening: A funeral [[chorale|chorale]]

stops.hear: Theme 2 returns, now in the minor, over a single note pulsing in the double basses
stops.happening: The consoling melody has become a lament. The pulse grows slower

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Only cellos and double basses, fading to nothing
stops.happening: The symphony ends where it began, in the dark lowest voices

notice: Theme 2 in its two forms: hopeful in the major, surrendered in the minor. The same notes, the opposite meaning.
The pulse in the double basses answers the heartbeat note of the second movement. Here it slows and stops.
The silence after the last note is part of the piece. Do not skip to the next track.

notes.title: A hidden trick
notes.body: No single instrument plays the opening melody. Its notes are shared out alternately between the first and second violins, and the tune exists only when the two are combined. When the melody returns later, Tchaikovsky gives it plainly to the first violins.

threads.title: The falling line
threads.body: Almost every important melody in the symphony moves downward.

threads.title: The pulse
threads.body: A repeated single note in the second movement returns in the double basses at the end, slows, and stops.

threads.title: Darkness to darkness
threads.body: The symphony begins and ends in the lowest instruments.

threads.title: Extreme dynamics
threads.body: The score runs from pppppp to fff.

threads.title: The reversed order
threads.body: Triumph arrives in the “wrong” place, so the finale feels like a truth revealed.
